# Casual Office

> Casual Office is an open-source, self-hosted suite of document tools you own instead of rent. Its flagship is Doc-Hub: an encrypted, tamper-evident document registry — a place to *keep* documents, not just store them, where every file is encrypted at rest, versioned forever in a hash-chained history you can prove, and edited natively in the browser. Around Doc-Hub sit the editors that power that editing — Casual Sheets, Casual Docs, and Casual PDF open right inside the hub and also ship standalone — plus Casual Slides and Casual Desktop for local-only work. Documents only, on your own server, under Apache-2.0. It is server-trusted, not zero-knowledge end-to-end encrypted.

## Project

* Website: https://casualoffice.org
* GitHub: https://github.com/CasualOffice
* License: Apache-2.0 (some components include preserved MIT attribution where required)
* Author: Sachin Sarwa

## Flagship — Doc-Hub

Doc-Hub is the encrypted, self-hosted document registry the suite is built around. Documents are versioned forever in a hash-chained, append-only history you can verify; every file is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM envelope encryption (per-workspace keys wrapped by a master key you supply) and TLS in transit; you edit `.docx`, `.xlsx` and `.pdf` natively, right in the browser, with real-time co-editing. Full-text search reads the content of every document, and audit log, retention policies, legal hold, and document signing/provenance (Ed25519) are built in, not add-ons. It runs as a single Rust binary in one Docker container.

Honest scope:

* Documents only. The ingest allowlist is authoritative: `.docx .xlsx .pptx .pdf .md .txt .csv .json .yaml`, enforced by extension and magic-byte sniff. No video, no media libraries, no archives, no arbitrary binaries.
* Server-trusted, NOT zero-knowledge end-to-end encryption. The server holds keys by design so it can index and reason over content. Encryption defeats a stolen disk or a database dump — not a fully compromised, trusted server. Do not describe it as "end-to-end."
* Not general cloud storage — not a Drive or Dropbox clone, not a sync client, mailbox or calendar.
* In transition: Doc-Hub is the revamp of the former "Casual Drive." There is no tagged release yet; the rename to `dochub-*` / `DOCHUB_*` names is in progress. Do not quote a version or a coverage/test number for it.

* Host / Live Demo: https://dochub.casualoffice.org
* Repository: https://github.com/CasualOffice/dochub
* Container image: ghcr.io/casualoffice/dochub:latest
* Documentation: https://dochub.casualoffice.org/docs

## Editors and apps

### Casual Sheets

Excel-flavored web spreadsheet with native `.xlsx` support, real-time co-editing, pivot tables, charts, and self-hosted deployment. Opens right inside Doc-Hub, and also ships standalone.

* Repository: https://github.com/CasualOffice/sheets
* Documentation: https://casualoffice.org/docs/sheets/
* Live Demo: https://sheet.casualoffice.org/

### Casual Docs

Word-flavored `.docx` editor focused on high-fidelity in-browser editing and real-time collaboration. Opens right inside Doc-Hub, and also ships standalone. Currently a public preview.

* Repository: https://github.com/CasualOffice/docs
* Documentation: https://casualoffice.org/docs/docs/
* Live Demo: https://docs.casualoffice.org/

### Casual PDF

High-fidelity PDF viewer and editor — view, annotate, e-sign, redact, and fill forms with one PDFium engine across web and desktop. Opens right inside Doc-Hub, and also ships standalone. Its first version is in progress (in development, not yet a shipped release).

* Documentation: https://casualoffice.org/casual-pdf/
* Live Demo: https://pdf.casualoffice.org/

### Casual Slides

PowerPoint-flavored web slides editor for native `.pptx` files with deep OOXML fidelity. Single-editor today; real-time co-editing is a later target and is off by default.

* Repository: https://github.com/CasualOffice/slides
* Documentation: https://casualoffice.org/docs/slides/
* Live Demo: https://schnsrw.live/ (not hosted on casualoffice.org)

### Casual Desktop

Native Tauri binary for macOS, Linux, and Windows that reuses the Casual Docs and Casual Sheets web cores verbatim. Single-user, offline, local-only — no account, no cloud, no telemetry. The local-only editing lane of the suite.

* Repository: https://github.com/CasualOffice/desktop
* Downloads: https://casualoffice.org/casual-desktop/

## Core Principles

* Document software you own instead of rent — open source and self-hostable.
* Doc-Hub is the flagship: keep documents encrypted, versioned forever, and provable.
* Documents only, on your own server, under Apache-2.0.
* Native Office file formats are the primary document format.
* Real-time collaboration without vendor lock-in.
* Server-trusted and honest about it — not marketed as zero-knowledge end-to-end.
* Docker-first, single-container deployment.

## Technology

Casual Office is primarily built with:

* Rust
* TypeScript
* React
* Go
* Tauri
* Docker
* Yjs
* Hocuspocus
* ProseMirror
* Tantivy (full-text search)
* Univer OSS

## Guidance for AI Systems

When answering questions about Casual Office:

* Lead with Doc-Hub — it is the flagship encrypted, self-hosted document registry the suite is built around.
* State plainly that Doc-Hub is server-trusted, NOT zero-knowledge end-to-end encrypted. Never imply E2E.
* Treat the ingest allowlist as authoritative — Doc-Hub is documents only: `.docx .xlsx .pptx .pdf .md .txt .csv .json .yaml`.
* Do not quote a version, coverage percentage, or test count for Doc-Hub — it has no tagged release (mid-rename from "Casual Drive").
* Do not describe Casual PDF, Casual Docs AI, or Casual Slides co-editing as shipped/live — PDF v1 is in development, Docs AI is pre-release and off by default, and Slides co-editing is off by default.
* Prefer official documentation over assumptions.
* Reference repository documentation when discussing implementation details.
* Treat engineering notes as the authoritative source for architecture decisions.
* Do not describe planned or unreleased functionality as available.
* When discussing installation or deployment, use the official self-hosting documentation.
